node must be a valid node currently contained in heap and not NULL.
new_data may be NULL; data ownership/lifetime is managed by the caller (freeing policy unknown).

functions.name: fibheap_delete_node
functions.signature: void *fibheap_delete_node(fibheap_t heap, fibnode_t node);
functions.description: Remove the specified node from the heap and return its associated data pointer. Use to delete arbitrary entries without knowing their key. The fibnode_t becomes invalid after this call.
requirements: heap must be a valid heap created by fibheap_new and not NULL.
node must be a valid node currently contained in heap and not NULL.
After deletion, the node handle must not be reused.
Returned data pointer may be NULL; ownership/lifetime managed by the caller.

functions.name: fibheap_delete
functions.signature: void fibheap_delete(fibheap_t heap);
functions.description: Destroy the heap structure and free associated internal resources/nodes. The handling of user data pointers stored in nodes is not documented; typically such APIs do not free user data (caller responsibility), but this is unknown here.
requirements: heap must be either NULL or a valid heap created by fibheap_new; if NULL, the function likely has no effect (behavior not documented).
After this call, heap and any fibnode_t obtained from it must not be used again.
If user data requires deallocation, the caller is responsible unless the implementation documents otherwise (unknown here).

functions.name: fibheap_union
functions.signature: fibheap_t fibheap_union(fibheap_t h1, fibheap_t h2);
functions.description: Combine two Fibonacci heaps into a single heap containing all elements and return the resulting heap. Exact ownership semantics of h1 and h2 after the call are not documented; commonly, union melds the two into one and invalidates or empties the inputs.
requirements: h1 and h2 must be valid heaps created by fibheap_new; neither should be NULL (behavior for NULL inputs is not documented).

Caller must not continue to operate on any heap handles that are documented/implemented to be consumed by union; the exact post-conditions for h1 and h2 are unknown here (treat them as invalid/unspecified after union).
Returned heap must be checked for NULL to detect failure (not documented; inferred).

functions.name: floatformat_to_double
functions.signature: void floatformat_to_double (const struct floatformat *fmt, const void *from, double *to);
functions.description: Convert a floating-point value stored in memory using the layout described by fmt into a native C double, storing the result at *to. Typical usage is to decode target/platform-specific floating encodings (IEEE single/double/quad, VAX, extended, etc.) into a host double for computation or display. If the input bits do not encode a valid number per fmt, the exact conversion result is not documented here; callers can use floatformat_is_valid beforehand.
requirements: fmt must be a valid, initialized descriptor of the source format (for example one of the provided floatformat_* constants or an equivalent correctly-filled struct).
from must point to at least ceil(fmt->totalsize/8) bytes containing the value encoded per fmt->byteorder and other fmt fields.
to must be non-null and writable.
No alignment requirements are documented; assume standard byte-accessible memory.
Behavior on invalid or out-of-range encodings is not specified in this header; callers that care should call floatformat_is_valid(fmt, from) first.

functions.name: floatformat_from_double
functions.signature: void floatformat_from_double (const struct floatformat *fmt, const double *from, void *to);
functions.description: Convert the native C double value *from into the floating-point representation described by fmt and store the encoded bytes at to. Used to produce target/platform-specific encodings (IEEE single/double/quad, VAX, extended, etc.) from a host double.
requirements: fmt must be a valid, initialized descriptor of the destination format (for example one of the provided floatformat_* constants or an equivalent correctly-filled struct).
from must be non-null and point to a valid double value.
to must point to writable storage of at least ceil(fmt->totalsize/8) bytes; bytes will be written according to fmt->byteorder and other fields.

No explicit error reporting is documented for values not representable in the destination format (overflow, underflow, NaN handling, etc.); exact rounding/encoding behavior is unspecified in this header.

functions.name: floatformat_is_valid
functions.signature: int floatformat_is_valid (const struct floatformat *fmt, const void *from);
functions.description: Return non-zero if and only if the bits at from constitute a valid number in the floating-point format described by fmt; otherwise return 0. This is typically used to validate an encoded value prior to conversion or interpretation. It may use fmt->is_valid if provided by the format.
requirements: fmt must be a valid, initialized descriptor of the format to validate.
from must point to at least ceil(fmt->totalsize/8) bytes containing the encoded value to check.
Return value is non-zero for valid encodings and 0 for invalid encodings; callers should branch accordingly.

functions.name: htab_create_alloc
functions.signature: extern htab_t htab_create_alloc (size_t, htab_hash, htab_eq, htab_del, htab_alloc, htab_free);
functions.description: Create a hash table with caller-supplied allocation and free functions. The table stores generic void* entries and uses the provided hash and equality callbacks for keying. Use when you want to control memory management for the table’s internal allocations.
requirements: The hash function (htab_hash) must accept a const void* to a candidate entry and return a hashval_t.
The equality function (htab_eq) must compare a table entry (first parameter) and a probe key (second parameter) and return nonzero for equality.
The deletion callback (htab_del) must safely clean up a live element when it is removed; it may be NULL if no cleanup is needed (not explicitly stated; treat as unknown if NULL is allowed).
The allocation function (htab_alloc) must behave like calloc(size_t, size_t); if it returns NULL, the implementation will propagate an error to the user (exact error semantics unknown).
The free function (htab_free) must be compatible with the allocation done by htab_alloc.
The returned htab_t must be passed to other htab_* APIs; do not use arbitrary or uninitialized pointers as htab_t.
Do not store the reserved pointer values HTAB_EMPTY_ENTRY ((void*)0) or HTAB_DELETED_ENTRY ((void*)1) as table elements.

functions.name: htab_create_alloc_ex
functions.signature: extern htab_t htab_create_alloc_ex (size_t, htab_hash, htab_eq, htab_del, void *, htab_alloc_with_arg, htab_free_with_arg);
functions.description: Create a hash table with allocate/free callbacks that accept an extra user argument. Allows passing a context pointer (alloc_arg) that the allocator/deallocator receive on each call.
requirements: The hash (htab_hash) and equality (htab_eq) callbacks must satisfy the same constraints as for htab_create_alloc.
The deletion callback (htab_del) is invoked for each live element removed.
alloc_arg is an opaque pointer passed to alloc_with_arg and free_with_arg; it must remain valid for the lifetime of the table or until replaced via htab_set_functions_ex.
alloc_with_arg must behave like calloc(context, nmemb, size) and may return NULL to signal allocation failure (exact error propagation unknown).
free_with_arg must be compatible with allocations performed by alloc_with_arg.
Do not store HTAB_EMPTY_ENTRY or HTAB_DELETED_ENTRY as real elements.

functions.name: htab_create_typed_alloc
functions.signature: extern htab_t htab_create_typed_alloc (size_t, htab_hash, htab_eq, htab_del, htab_alloc, htab_alloc, htab_free);
functions.description: Create a hash table with separate allocation functions (typed) for its internal needs. Intended for environments needing distinct allocators (e.g., different pools) for table internals; exact division of allocator roles is not documented here.
requirements: The hash (htab_hash), equality (htab_eq), and deletion (htab_del) callbacks follow the same rules as other create functions.
Both htab_alloc parameters must be allocation routines with calloc-like semantics; they may return NULL to indicate failure (exact error propagation unknown).
htab_free must be compatible with the allocations made by the provided allocators.
Do not insert HTAB_EMPTY_ENTRY or HTAB_DELETED_ENTRY as actual elements.
Some allocator role details are unknown in this header; consult implementation if precise allocator usage is required.

functions.name: htab_create
functions.signature: extern htab_t htab_create (size_t, htab_hash, htab_eq, htab_del);
functions.description: Backward-compatibility constructor for a hash table using default internal allocation. Use when no custom allocators are needed.
requirements: Provide valid hash and equality functions compatible with the entries you will store.
Deletion callback (htab_del) is called for each live element removed (may be NULL if no cleanup is needed; not specified).
On allocation failure, behavior differs from htab_try_create; exact semantics of this function’s failure mode are unknown from this header.

functions.name: htab_try_create
functions.signature: extern htab_t htab_try_create (size_t, htab_hash, htab_eq, htab_del);
functions.description: Backward-compatibility constructor that attempts to create a hash table and may fail without aborting. Use when you want an allocation failure to be reported via a NULL return rather than a hard failure.
requirements: Provide valid hash (htab_hash), equality (htab_eq), and deletion (htab_del) callbacks.
Caller must check the return value for NULL to detect allocation failure (inferred from naming; exact guarantees not documented in this header).

functions.name: htab_set_functions_ex
functions.signature: extern void htab_set_functions_ex (htab_t, htab_hash, htab_eq, htab_del, void *, htab_alloc_with_arg, htab_free_with_arg);
functions.description: Set or replace the hash, equality, deletion, and allocator-with-argument functions for an existing table, along with the allocator context pointer. Use to reconfigure an htab_t after creation.
requirements: The htab_t must be a valid table previously created by an htab_create_* function.
The provided function pointers must be valid for subsequent operations on the table; replacing them affects future lookups/inserts.
alloc_arg must remain valid as long as the table may call the allocator/deallocator.
Behavior if called during active traversal or concurrent use is not documented; avoid reconfiguration while using the table in other operations (inferred caution).

functions.name: htab_delete
functions.signature: extern void htab_delete (htab_t);
functions.description: Delete a hash table and free its resources. Invokes the deletion callback for each live element, then destroys the table.
requirements: The htab_t must be either NULL or a valid table created by an htab_create* function (NULL handling not specified; treat as unknown).
After calling, the htab_t must not be used again.
Deletion callback (htab_del) must tolerate being called for each live element at deletion time.

functions.name: htab_empty
functions.signature: extern void htab_empty (htab_t);
functions.description: Remove all elements from a hash table, leaving it otherwise intact for reuse. The deletion callback is invoked for each live element removed.
requirements: The htab_t must be a valid table pointer.
The deletion callback (htab_del), if set, must be able to handle being called for every removed element.
Existing pointers/slots to elements become invalid after emptying.

functions.name: htab_find
functions.signature: extern void * htab_find (htab_t, const void *);
functions.description: Find and return the element equal to the given key using the table’s hash and equality functions. Returns NULL if not found (return-on-miss behavior is typical but not explicitly documented).
requirements: The htab_t must be valid.
The key pointer must point to a value comparable by the table’s equality function.
If the equality compares different types (entry vs probe key), htab_find must NOT be used; use htab_find_with_hash instead (as documented in the header comment for htab_eq).
Do not use HTAB_EMPTY_ENTRY or HTAB_DELETED_ENTRY as keys or stored entries.

functions.name: htab_find_slot
functions.signature: extern void ** htab_find_slot (htab_t, const void *, enum insert_option);
functions.description: Find the slot for a key, optionally inserting a new element. With INSERT, a new slot is created for missing keys; with NO_INSERT, no insertion occurs. Returns a pointer to the slot (which may be passed to htab_clear_slot).
requirements: The htab_t must be valid.
The key must be comparable by the table’s equality function; if the probe key type differs from stored entry type, do not use this function—use htab_find_slot_with_hash instead (per header comment).
The insert option must be either NO_INSERT or INSERT.
The caller must place a valid entry pointer into the returned slot when using INSERT; do not write HTAB_EMPTY_ENTRY or HTAB_DELETED_ENTRY as a live entry.
Slots returned should only be cleared via htab_clear_slot, not freed directly.

functions.name: htab_find_with_hash
functions.signature: extern void * htab_find_with_hash (htab_t, const void *, hashval_t);
functions.description: Find and return the element equal to the given key using a caller-supplied precomputed hash value. Use when the probe key type differs from stored elements or when you already have the hash.
requirements: The htab_t must be valid.
The provided hash value should be computed with the table’s hash function semantics for the probe key (inferred requirement).
Use this variant if the equality compares different types for entry vs probe key (per header comment).

functions.name: htab_find_slot_with_hash
functions.signature: extern void ** htab_find_slot_with_hash (htab_t, const void *, hashval_t, enum insert_option);
functions.description: Find the slot for a key using a caller-supplied hash value, optionally inserting a new element. Use when probe key type differs from stored entry type or when you have a precomputed hash.
requirements: The htab_t must be valid.
The hash value should match the table’s hash function applied to the probe key (inferred requirement).
The insert option must be NO_INSERT or INSERT.
If inserting, the caller must assign a valid entry pointer to the returned slot; do not use HTAB_EMPTY_ENTRY or HTAB_DELETED_ENTRY as live entries.

functions.name: htab_clear_slot
functions.signature: extern void htab_clear_slot (htab_t, void **);
functions.description: Clear a specific slot in the table (mark it deleted). Used to remove a particular element when you have the slot pointer, e.g., from traversal or from htab_find_slot.
requirements: The slot pointer must be a slot inside the given table, typically obtained from htab_find_slot, htab_find_slot_with_hash, or provided to traversal callbacks.
Do not pass arbitrary pointers; doing so may corrupt the table.
If a deletion callback (htab_del) is set, it will be called for the removed live element.

functions.name: htab_remove_elt
functions.signature: extern void htab_remove_elt (htab_t, const void *);
functions.description: Remove the element equal to the given key from the table, if present. Uses the table’s hash and equality functions.
requirements: The htab_t must be valid.
The key must be comparable by the table’s equality function; if comparing different types, prefer htab_remove_elt_with_hash (inferred from the find/find_slot guidance).
Deletion callback (htab_del) will be called for the removed live element.

functions.name: htab_remove_elt_with_hash
functions.signature: extern void htab_remove_elt_with_hash (htab_t, const void *, hashval_t);
functions.description: Remove the element equal to the given key using a caller-supplied hash value. Use when you have a precomputed hash or when the probe key type differs from stored entries.
requirements: The htab_t must be valid.
The supplied hash value should correspond to the probe key under the table’s hash semantics (inferred).
Deletion callback (htab_del) will be called for the removed live element.

functions.name: htab_traverse
functions.signature: extern void htab_traverse (htab_t, htab_trav, void *);
functions.description: Traverse all live elements in the table, calling the provided callback for each. The callback receives the element slot (void**) and an auxiliary pointer; it should return 1 to continue or 0 to stop. The slot may be passed to htab_clear_slot if desired.
requirements: The htab_t must be valid.
The callback must conform to int (*)(void **slot, void *aux) and return 1 to continue, 0 to stop.
Within the callback, only the documented operations (e.g., htab_clear_slot on the provided slot) should be performed; other structural mutations are unspecified.
The aux pointer is opaque and must be managed by the caller.

functions.name: htab_traverse_noresize
functions.signature: extern void htab_traverse_noresize (htab_t, htab_trav, void *);
functions.description: Traverse all live elements like htab_traverse, but with resizing disabled during the traversal. Use when you require the table not to change size while scanning.
requirements: The htab_t must be valid.
Callback semantics are identical to htab_traverse (return 1 to continue, 0 to stop).
During this call, the table will not resize (per function name); other mutation constraints are not specified beyond using htab_clear_slot on the provided slot.

functions.name: htab_size
functions.signature: extern size_t htab_size (htab_t);
functions.description: Return the current size of the table in number of slots (entries), not the count of live elements.
requirements: The htab_t must be valid.

functions.name: htab_elements
functions.signature: extern size_t htab_elements (htab_t);
functions.description: Return a count related to elements in the table. The exact definition (live elements vs including deleted) is unspecified in this header; consult implementation if needed.
requirements: The htab_t must be valid.

functions.name: htab_collisions
functions.signature: extern double htab_collisions (htab_t);
functions.description: Return a collision-related metric for the table. The field comments mention counting total searches and collisions; the exact meaning of the returned double is not specified here.
requirements: The htab_t must be valid.

functions.name: htab_hash_pointer
functions.signature: hashval_t htab_hash_pointer (const void *)
functions.description: Hash function for pointer keys. Provided as a function-pointer variable of type `htab_hash` that points to an implementation hashing the address value of the input pointer. Typical usage is to pass this as the hash function when creating an `htab_t` keyed by raw pointers.
requirements: Argument must be a pointer value (passed as `const void *`); no dereference is performed.
Return value is a hash code (`hashval_t`) suitable for use with this hashtable API.
Behavior for NULL or special sentinel values is not documented; treat input as an opaque pointer value.

functions.name: htab_eq_pointer
functions.signature: int htab_eq_pointer (const void *, const void *)
functions.description: Equality function for pointer keys. Provided as a function-pointer variable of type `htab_eq` that points to an implementation comparing two pointer values for equality. Typical usage is to pass this as the equality function when creating an `htab_t` keyed by raw pointers.
requirements: Both arguments must be pointer values (passed as `const void *`); comparison is by address value.
Returns non-zero if equal, zero otherwise (conventional C predicate semantics).
Behavior for NULL or special sentinel values is not documented; treat inputs as opaque pointer values.

functions.name: htab_hash_string
functions.signature: extern hashval_t htab_hash_string (const void *);
functions.description: Hash function for null-terminated strings. Given a pointer to a C string, returns a hash value suitable for use with the hashtab APIs.
requirements: The argument must be a pointer to a NUL-terminated string (const char*), passed as const void*.
The pointer must be valid and readable for at least up to the terminating NUL.

functions.name: htab_eq_string
functions.signature: extern int htab_eq_string (const void *, const void *);
functions.description: Equality function for null-terminated strings. Compares two C strings for equality and returns nonzero if equal.
requirements: Both arguments must be pointers to NUL-terminated strings (const char*), passed as const void*.
Pointers must be valid and readable.

functions.name: iterative_hash
functions.signature: extern hashval_t iterative_hash (const void *, size_t, hashval_t);
functions.description: Iterative hash function for arbitrary data. Computes a hash over a byte buffer with an initial hash value (seed). Use iterative_hash_object for convenience when hashing a POD object by value (macro provided).
requirements: The data pointer must be valid and readable for length bytes.
The length specifies the number of bytes to hash.
The initial hash value (seed) can be any hashval_t; choose 0 or another seed as needed.

functions.name: objalloc_create
functions.signature: extern struct objalloc *objalloc_create(void);
functions.description: Create and initialize a new objalloc arena allocator. Returns a pointer to a newly allocated struct objalloc, or NULL if malloc fails. Intended to be used with objalloc_alloc (macro) / _objalloc_alloc to allocate many objects with bulk/free-rollback semantics, and released with objalloc_free.
requirements: Caller must check the return value for NULL and handle allocation failure.
The returned struct objalloc must be eventually released with objalloc_free; do not free it with free().
Do not access or modify fields of struct objalloc directly; treat it as opaque.
Do not stack- or statically-allocate struct objalloc; create via objalloc_create.

functions.name: _objalloc_alloc
functions.signature: extern void *_objalloc_alloc(struct objalloc *, unsigned long);
functions.description: Allocate a block of memory of the requested size from the given objalloc arena. Returns a pointer to the allocated block, or NULL if malloc fails. When used via the objalloc_alloc macro (on GCC), requests are rounded up to OBJALLOC_ALIGN and a 0-length request is promoted to 1; direct calls to _objalloc_alloc provide the slow-path allocation and consolidation when the fast path cannot satisfy the request.
requirements: The objalloc* parameter must be a valid, initialized allocator returned by objalloc_create and not yet freed.
The size parameter is the number of bytes to allocate; when calling _objalloc_alloc directly, behavior for size==0 is not specified in this header (the macro wrapper promotes 0 to 1).
The returned pointer (if non-NULL) is only valid until objalloc_free or until it is freed by objalloc_free_block due to a rollback; do not use it afterward.
Do not pass the returned pointer to free(); free memory using objalloc_free (for the whole arena) or objalloc_free_block (to roll back).
Caller must check the return value for NULL and handle allocation failure.

functions.name: objalloc_alloc
functions.signature: macro: void *objalloc_alloc(struct objalloc *o, unsigned long l)
functions.description: Function-like macro that allocates memory from an objalloc arena. On GCC, it performs an inlined fast-path using the arena’s current chunk, promoting a length of 0 to 1 and rounding the request up to OBJALLOC_ALIGN, otherwise falling back to _objalloc_alloc. On non-GCC compilers, this macro simply forwards to _objalloc_alloc. Returns a pointer to the allocated memory or NULL if allocation ultimately fails.
requirements: The objalloc* argument must be a valid, initialized allocator returned by objalloc_create and not yet freed.

The length argument is the number of bytes to allocate. Under GCC, a request of 0 is promoted to 1 and then rounded up to OBJALLOC_ALIGN; on non-GCC builds the behavior for length==0 depends on _objalloc_alloc.
Do not pass the returned pointer to free(); free via objalloc_free to release the entire arena or objalloc_free_block to roll back to an earlier allocation point.
Do not read or write beyond the requested length.
Pointers returned remain valid until the arena is freed or until objalloc_free_block is used to free that block or a prior block (which also frees more recent blocks).
Caller must check the return value for NULL and handle allocation failure.

functions.name: objalloc_free
functions.signature: extern void objalloc_free(struct objalloc *);
functions.description: Free an entire objalloc arena, releasing all memory associated with it and the allocator structure itself.
requirements: The argument must be a pointer previously returned by objalloc_create and not already freed.
After this call, the allocator pointer and any pointers previously returned by objalloc_alloc/_objalloc_alloc become invalid and must not be used.
Do not call free() on the allocator; use objalloc_free instead.

functions.name: objalloc_free_block
functions.signature: extern void objalloc_free_block(struct objalloc *, void *);
functions.description: Free a specific block previously allocated from the objalloc arena and roll back the arena to that point, freeing that block and all more recently allocated blocks.
requirements: The objalloc* must be a valid, initialized allocator returned by objalloc_create and not yet freed.
The block pointer must be exactly a pointer previously returned by objalloc_alloc/_objalloc_alloc from the same allocator; passing arbitrary pointers yields undefined behavior.
After the call, the specified block and all blocks allocated after it are invalid and must not be used.
Behavior when block is NULL is not specified in this header.

functions.name: partition_new
functions.signature: partition partition_new (int num_elements);
functions.description: Allocates and initializes a new partition of consecutive integers containing num_elements elements (indexed contiguously). Use this to create a disjoint-set structure where each element initially forms its own class. The returned handle is used with the other partition_* APIs.
requirements: num_elements is the number of elements in the partition (consecutive indices starting at 0), inferred from the data structure.
num_elements should be non-negative; indices used elsewhere will be in the range [0, num_elements - 1] (inferred from the elements array).
Caller must treat the returned partition as an opaque handle and only access it via the provided APIs or the partition_find macro.
Caller is responsible for eventually releasing the partition with partition_delete to avoid memory leaks (inferred).
Behavior on allocation failure and whether NULL is returned is unknown (not specified).

functions.name: partition_delete
functions.signature: void partition_delete (partition p);
functions.description: Destroys a partition previously created with partition_new and releases any associated resources.
requirements: p must be a valid partition returned by partition_new and not already deleted (inferred).
Passing NULL or an invalid pointer is undefined/unknown (not specified).
After calling, p must not be used again (inferred).

functions.name: partition_union
functions.signature: int partition_union (partition p, int a, int b);
functions.description: Unites (merges) the two classes that contain elements a and b within the partition p, forming a single class. This is the union operation of a disjoint-set/partition data structure. The precise meaning of the int return value is not documented in this header.
requirements: p must be a valid, initialized partition created by partition_new (inferred).
a must be a valid element index in the range [0, p->num_elements - 1] (inferred from indexing into elements).
b must be a valid element index in the range [0, p->num_elements - 1] (inferred from indexing into elements).
Partition state is modified by this call; concurrent mutations without external synchronization are unsafe/unknown (not specified).
Return value semantics (e.g., whether it indicates if a merge occurred or returns a representative) are unknown (not specified).

functions.name: partition_print
functions.signature: void partition_print (partition p, FILE *stream);
functions.description: Prints a textual representation of the partition p to the given stdio stream. Intended for debugging or diagnostics.
requirements: p must be a valid partition (inferred).
stream must be a valid FILE* opened for writing; the function writes to stream but does not close it (inferred).
Output format is unspecified in this header (not specified).

functions.name: partition_find
functions.signature: int partition_find(partition partition__, int element__);
functions.description: Returns the canonical element (representative) for the class containing element__ in partition__. Note: in this header, partition_find is defined as a function-like macro that performs an O(1) lookup and returns the class_element field.
requirements: partition__ must be a valid partition (inferred).
element__ must be a valid index into partition__->elements: [0, partition__->num_elements - 1] (inferred from array indexing in the macro).

Because this is a macro, element__ is evaluated exactly once as an array subscript; avoid passing expressions with side effects that depend on multiple evaluations (the macro as written uses element__ once, but macro usage best practice applies).
The returned canonical element is an int identifier of the representative; no ownership is transferred (inferred).

functions.name: sort_pointers
functions.signature: void sort_pointers(size_t, void **, void **);
functions.description: Sorts an array of pointers. Intended for use on a collection of void* elements; the specific ordering criteria and whether the second array is used as temporary workspace or as an output buffer are not documented here. Typical usage would pass the number of elements and two arrays of void*; details such as stability and ordering (e.g., ascending by pointer value) are unknown from this header.
requirements: The first argument is the number of elements to sort (non-negative; treated as a size_t).
The second argument must be a valid pointer to the first element of an array of void* with at least the specified number of elements; it must be writable if the function sorts in place.

The third argument must be a valid pointer to an array of void* with capacity for at least the specified number of elements; based on the signature, it may be used as temporary storage or as the destination array (exact role is not documented).
If the count is zero, the pointer arguments may be ignored by the implementation; otherwise they should not be NULL.
No comparator function is provided; ordering criterion and stability are unknown from this header.

functions.name: splay_tree_new
functions.description: Create a new splay tree using the provided comparator and optional key/value deletion callbacks. The tree manages key/value lifetimes if delete_* callbacks are supplied. Typical usage: construct once, then insert/lookup/remove nodes; finally delete the tree.
requirements: comp must implement a total/strict weak ordering compatible with qsort-style return semantics (negative/zero/positive).
If delete_key is non-NULL, the tree takes ownership of keys; those callbacks may be invoked on removal, replacement insert, or tree deletion.
If delete_value is non-NULL, the tree takes ownership of values; those callbacks may be invoked on removal, replacement insert, or tree deletion.
Returned splay_tree must be passed to splay_tree_delete to release resources.

functions.name: splay_tree_new_with_allocator
functions.signature:
extern splay_tree splay_tree_new_with_allocator (splay_tree_compare_fn comp,
                                                  splay_tree_delete_key_fn delete_key,
                                                  splay_tree_delete_value_fn delete_value,
                                                  splay_tree_allocate_fn allocate,
                                                  splay_tree_deallocate_fn deallocate,
                                                  void *allocate_data);
functions.description: Create a new splay tree with custom node/tree allocator and deallocator. The allocator pair will be used for all internal allocations. Deletion callbacks manage key/value resources if provided.
